The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, August 2, 1937

Huge Extortion
Case Re-Opened

Prisoner Admits Guilt
In Court; $244,000
Said Involved

Kong Zau-tseu, alias Kong Zu,
42, who was arrested last week by
Chinese detectives Yang Hsin-
kwang and Chang Yun-hung of
the Crime Branch Headquarters
in Nanking in connection with ex-
tortion activities in Shanghai to-
gether with an ex-detective of the
Settlement police, during the last
few years, when brought to the
First Special District Court this
morning admitted that he extort-
ed large amounts from various
people but not as much as the
$244,000 the police allege.

According to the evidence pro-
duced by Municipal Advocate Pau'
Y. R'u, who charged the man with
extortion, Kong was connected
with no less than 14 known cases
of extortion involving hundreds of
thousands of dollars. Among his
near victim was George "Playboy"
Hardoon whom Kong tried to get
in his hands and instigate a law-
suit against Mrs. Hardoon. His
victims number some 50 wealthy
persons in Shanghai, according to
the advocate. No witnesses were
present in court, however, and the
advocate requested the judge to
name those whom he would like
to question so that they could be
asked to come to court during
the hearings.

It is alleged that Kong together
with the ex-detective Shen Zo-
ching, who was sentenced to five
years in jail last March, made in-
timate contacts with rich people
and after digging up scandals
ranging from rape to disappropria-
tion extorted money with the aid
of gangsters. By this means it
is estimated that during four years
they extorted more than $500,000

Among Kong's victims was Miss
Shih Ching-yen, a well-known
actress of the Peiping stage. It
is also alleged that the two chief
criminals opened a law office on
Rue Auguste Boppe in the Con-
cession formerly known as the Chu
Kwang Law Office. Out of the
14 known cases against him only
three extortion cases involving in
all $244,000 were brought against
the man today. Hearing was re-
manded until next week.

巨额勒索案
重审

被告当庭认罪；
涉案金额据称
达24.4万美元

孔祖泽（Kong Zau-tseu），又名孔祖（Kong Zu），42岁，上周由南京刑事科总部的中国侦探杨新光（Yang Hsin-kwang）和张云洪（Chang Yun-hung）逮捕，涉嫌与一名前租界巡捕房侦探在过去几年中于上海进行勒索活动。今晨在第一特区地方法院受审时，他承认曾向多人勒索巨款，但数额并非警方指控的24.4万美元。

根据负责以勒索罪起诉该男子的工部局检察官鲍尔（Pau' Y. R'u，音译）提供的证据，孔某涉及不少于14起已知的勒索案件，涉案金额达数十万美元。其受害者中包括乔治·“花花公子”·哈同（George "Playboy" Hardoon），孔某试图控制他并煽动其对哈同夫人提起诉讼。据检察官称，其受害者包括上海约50名富豪。然而，法庭上并无证人出庭，检察官请求法官指定他希望讯问的人员名单，以便在听证期间传唤他们到庭。

据称，孔某与去年三月被判入狱五年的前侦探沈佐清（Shen Zo-ching，音译）勾结，与富人建立密切关系，在挖掘出从强奸到挪用公款等各种丑闻后，借助帮派分子的力量勒索钱财。据估计，四年间他们通过此种手段勒索了超过50万美元。

孔某的受害者中包括著名北平舞台女演员石静艳（Shih Ching-yen，音译）。另据称，这两名主犯在租界奥古斯特·博佩路（Rue Auguste Boppe）开设了一家律师事务所，该处此前被称为朱光律师事务所（Chu Kwang Law Office）。在针对他的14起已知案件中，今日仅就其中三起总计涉及24.4万美元的勒索案对该男子提起诉讼。案件审理延期至下周。

As before stated, this case was initiated through
a private prosecution brought against Sung by his accomplice
Kiang Chao-chow. However, as the facts outlined in the
prosecution indicated a criminal charge, the Court, after its
receipt of this prosecution, referred the matter to the Central
Police Station for investigation. As a result of enquiries
conducted by Asst. Supt. Loh Lien-kwe and other police officers,
the following cases which were managed by Sung Sao-ching and
his accomplice Kiang Chao-chow, who is now at large, since
the winter of 1931 up to March last year, were brought to light:-
(1) Extortion of $40,000 from Wu Teng-ying (吴登瀛). Sung
only gave $12,500 to Wu's sister, Sung Wu-sz (孙吴氏),
and the rest he misappropriated. This aroused the
dissatisfaction of Sung Wu-sz who afterwards wrote a
letter to this effect to the Huchow Guild.
(2) Extortion of $70,000 from Chow Hsiang-yung (周湘云).
Sung only gave $5,000 to Wu Ngoh-hu (吴月娥), while
the rest was misappropriated by him together with Tang
Kia-pang (唐家鹏), the late Manager of the Great
World Amusement Resort on Avenue Edward VII.
(3) Extortion of $40,000 from Sze Tuh-tse (施德之).
(4) Extortion of $67,000 from Loh Kwan-tseng (罗冠曾).
$30,000 was given to Loh Chu-shang (罗祖尚), while the
remainder was taken by Sung.
(5) Extortion of $20,000 from Hsu Mou-chong (徐懋昌).
$3,000 only was given to Pan Chao-sz (潘赵氏), the
mother of Pan Sih-yen (潘世彦).
(6) Extortion of $47,000 from Chiang Yang-sz (蒋杨氏).
According to the lengthy judgment handed down
by Judge Chien Hung-nieh (钱洪业), Chief of the Criminal

although some of these crimes were committed by the accused

157 (Section 2), 55, 37 (Section 2), 42 (Sections 2 and 3),
2 (First Half of Section 1), and 168 of the Criminal Code
and Articles 291 (First Half) and 293 (Section 1) of the
Code of Criminal Procedure.

如前所述，此案是由宋的同伙江肇周对宋提起自诉而引发的。然而，由于自诉书中陈述的事实表明涉及刑事犯罪，法院在收到此自诉后，将此事移交中央捕房调查。经副督察长罗连桂（Loh Lien-kwe，音译）及其他警官进行的查询，查明了宋少卿与其目前在逃的同伙江肇周自1931年冬至去年三月期间经手的以下案件：

(2) 向周湘云勒索70,000美元。宋仅将5,000美元交给吴月娥（Wu Ngoh-hu），其余款项被他与爱多亚路大世界游乐场前经理唐家鹏共同侵吞。
(3) 向施德之勒索40,000美元。
(4) 向罗冠曾勒索67,000美元。其中30,000美元交给罗祖尚（Loh Chu-shang），其余被宋拿走。
(5) 向徐懋昌勒索20,000美元。仅将3,000美元交给潘世彦之母潘赵氏（Pan Chao-sz）。
(6) 向蒋杨氏勒索47,000美元。
根据上海第一特区地方法院刑事庭庭长钱洪业法官作出的长篇判决，虽然被告的部分犯罪行为发生在新刑法颁布之前，但根据旧刑法，其在包揽他人诉讼后的勒索行为仍应受到惩罚。

Eastern Times and other local newspapers :-

THE CASE AG/INST SUNG SAO CHING CONCLUDED

Yesterday afternoon the case against Sung Sao-ohing (孫 少卿) (an ex-C.D.C. of the S.M.P.) and his wife, Sung Tsu Sz (孫 朱氏), for extortion and contracting the management of lawsuits of another was again heard at the Shanghai First Special District Court before Judge Chien Hung-nieh (錢 鴻業).
Assistant Municipal Advocate Wong Yao-daung (王 耀堂) addressed the Court, saying: "During the period of remand, the Police have located witness Faung Nian-shuan (方 念萱) who is at present in Court ready to give evidence."
Witness Faung Nian-shuan then made the following statement to the Court :- "Zung Faung Sz(陳方氏) alias Tsu Faung Sz (朱 方 氏), who is the mother-in-law of the accused Sung Sao-ching, is also my aunt. After the conclusion of the Shanghai Hostilities of 1932, I was unemployed and depended on Sung Sao-ching for a living. Later I worked in the Zu Kwang Law Office (祖光法律事務所) jointly formed by Sung Sao-ching and Kiang Chao-chow (江 肇 周). At first the law office was located at No. 19 Chih Oo Faung (輯 五 坊), Rue Porte de l'Ouest, but it was later removed to No. 414 Rue Auguste Boppe. The crimes for which charges are brought by the Police were all managed by Kiang Chao-chow and Sung Sao-ching. The method they used to extort money was either to file a lawsuit or to send threatening letters, throw night soil, intimidate through the telephone, etc. Subsequently, one Ling Ya-yeh (林 雅 月), a female neighbour of mine, was abandoned by Koh Vee-ih (許 唯 一), manager of the Watson Mineral Water Factory, after having been seduced by him. Through my introduction, her case was taken up by Sung Sao-ching and Kiang Chao-chow who instituted legal proceedings against Koh Vee-ih in the Second Special District Court. At that time Sung and Kiang guaranteed that the lawsuit would end successfully. Nevertheless, the case was rejected by the Court as invalid, whereupon Koh Vee-ih filed a counter-action for false accusation. Tu Kwang (杜 況), husband of Ling Ya-yeh, approached me regarding the matter. Then I realized that Sung Sao-ching and Kiang Chao-chow would be caught sooner or later and that I would be implicated. For this reason, I surrendered myself to the Police."
Questioned by the Court, Sung Sao-ching and his wife still strongly denied the charges.
After debate between the Assistant Municipal Advocate and the defending counsel, Judge Chien Hung-nieh gave his decision sentencing Sung Sao-ching to 5 years' imprisonment and a fine of $1,000 for the offence of extortion, while Sung Tsu Sz was found guilty of perjury and sentenced to one year imprisonment.

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, MARCH 23, 1937

NEW CHARGES AGAINST MASTER EXTORTIONIST

When the police bring Sung San-ching, former S. M. P. detective and alleged master extortionist back in to the First Special District Court this morning, he will be confronted with three new charges, one of them involving the late Mr. Roy Talbot, prominent Nanking Road druggist of Sino-British extraction.

Approximately $50,000 is involved in all three charges. The one in which the name of Talbot is concerned accounts for $35,000 of that figure.

In the Talbot affair, according to the police, Sung will be charged with extortion by threat. The story of how he allegedly got this much is unique in local criminal history.

It is charged that a few years ago, the late Mr. Talbot, owner of Yau-hwa Medicine shop on Nan-king Road, put an anti-cholera medicine on the market under his own label. He registered this label with the government.

New Opportunity
Sung, it will be brought out in court, saw the possibilities of a large sale offered by this product and put a medicine on the market under a similar label.

Mr. Talbot is alleged to have written to Sung, protesting against the infringement and threatened action. This letter did the druggist dream that he was dealing with the alleged king of the local confidence men.

A few days later and Talbot had a case filed against him in the Nanking District Court for infringement on Sung's label.

Mr. Talbot filed a counter-suit in the 2nd Special District Court in the French Concession, the district in which Sung was making his anti-cholera medicine.

The cases were never completed in court, according to evidence at hand. Instead, Sung is alleged to have threatened Mr. Talbot on several occasions and that the latter finally settled for $35,000.

In the charge that will be presented yesterday, the police will contend that Sung and his gang delivered threats to the late Mr. Talbot by letter and telephone and that the latter actually called on the police to furnish him with an armed guard.

Attorney Assaulted
It will be further offered as evidence that on one occasion, Sung's men assaulted Mr. Talbot's attorney in the latter was leaving court. They threw a melon, hollowed out and filled with ordure, at the lawyer. It is said to have hit him and broken.

Mr. Talbot died some time ago but his business is still being carried on by members of his family.

One of the three new charges to be presented today involves $10,000. In this case it is alleged that Sung extorted that amount of money from an aged widow, Mrs. Tsiang Yeng-mei, who acted as a go-between for a businessman and her step-son. The latter attempted to get some of the money left Mrs. Tsiang by her husband. It is charged that Sung got most of it.

In the third new charge, it will be alleged that Sung swindled a local pawn-broker out of $5,000.

As matters now stand, six charges have been prepared against the alleged extortionist.

敲诈主犯面临新指控

当警方于今晨将前工部局警务处侦探、涉嫌敲诈主犯孙三庆（音译）带回第一特区地方法院时，他将面临三项新指控，其中一项涉及已故的罗伊·塔尔博特（Roy Talbot）先生，此人是南京路上著名的中英混血药剂师。

这三项指控涉及的总金额约为50,000元。其中涉及塔尔博特先生名下的案件占35,000元。

据警方称，在塔尔博特一案中，孙将被指控以威胁手段进行敲诈。据称他获取这笔巨款的手法在当地犯罪史上堪称独特。

指控称，几年前，南京路耀华药房老板已故塔尔博特先生以自己的品牌推出了一种霍乱预防药。他在政府注册了该商标。

新的机会
法庭将指出，孙看到了该产品巨大的销售潜力，并使用相似的商标将一种药品推向市场。

据称，塔尔博特先生曾致信孙，抗议侵权行为并威胁采取法律行动。这位药剂师做梦也没想到，他打交道的人竟是当地公认的诈骗团伙头目。

几天后，塔尔博特因侵犯孙的商标权而在南京地方法院被起诉。

塔尔博特先生在法租界（孙制造其霍乱预防药的地区）的第二特区地方法院提起反诉。

根据现有证据，这些案件从未在法庭上完结。相反，据称孙多次威胁塔尔博特先生，后者最终以35,000元达成和解。

在昨天提出的指控中，警方将主张孙及其团伙通过信件和电话向已故的塔尔博特先生发出威胁，且后者确实曾请求警方为其提供武装警卫。

律师遇袭
另将作为证据提出的是，有一次，孙的手下在塔尔博特先生的律师离开法庭时对其进行了袭击。他们向律师投掷了一个挖空并装满粪便的瓜。据说瓜击中了他并破裂。

塔尔博特先生已于不久前去世，但其生意仍由其家族成员经营。

今天提出的三项新指控之一涉及10,000元。在此案中，据称孙从一位年迈的寡妇蒋英梅（音译）夫人那里敲诈了这笔钱，她曾为一名商人和其继子充当中间人。后者试图获取蒋夫人丈夫留给她的部分钱财。据称，孙拿走了其中的大部分。

在第三项新指控中，据称孙诈骗了一名本地当铺老板5,000元。

截至目前，已针对这名涉嫌敲诈者准备了六项指控。

THE CASE AGAINST SUNG SAO CHING

Yesterday afternoon the case against Sung Sao Ching (孫少卿) (an ex-C.D.C. of the S.M.P.) for extortion and contracting the management of lawsuits of another was again heard at the Shanghai First Special District Court before Presiding Judge Chien Hung Nseh (錢鴻業).

Addressing the Court, Assistant Municipal Advocate Paul Y. Ru said: "In connection with the charge of extortion from Wu Teng Ying (吳登瀛), brought against the accused previously, the Municipal Police has now ascertained the number and the amount of the native order paid by the victim Wu Teng Ying as well as the name of the native bank where this order was negotiated. A detailed statement will be prepared for submission to the Court. Both Hsu Mou Chong (徐懋昌) and Pan Sih Yen (潘雪艷), the leading figures in connection with the charge of extortion from Hsu Mou Chong by the accused Sung Sao Ching, are present. The original text of the contract in connection with the 'Yao Tse Tsung (姚志春) Case' has been obtained, on which appears the signature of Sung Sao Ching. The Municipal Police now brings the following additional charges against the accused:-

"(1) Sometime in December of the 22nd Year (1933) of the Chinese Republic, the accused, by means of coercion, extorted a sum of $40,000 from one Mr. Sze Tuh Tse (施德之). The facts are as follows:- Sometime previous to this, Sze Tuh Tse discharged one of his coolies. In the name of the Chien Sou Hospital (濟善醫院), the discharged coolie, in collaboration with Sung Sao Ching, the accused, Wong Tseng Chuen (王振川), Van Liang Pah (樊良伯), Woo Yung Fu (吳雲甫) and others, filed a prosecution against Sze Tuh Tse in the Shanghai District Court, alleging that the anti-cholera liquid manufactured by him was an imitation of the Sze Tao Shih (施道世) anti-cholera liquid which they invented. In the course of this lawsuit, they even resorted to acts of coercion against Sze Tuh Tse and his lawyer Hsu Shih Hao (徐士浩), as a result of which they were able to obtain $40,000 from the victim. The Bubbling Well Police Station was notified at that time of their unlawful actions by Mr. 'Ro-Ber-S' (羅勃斯), son-in-law of Sze Tuh Tse.

"The records taken down by the Police Station at that time are now here for examination by the Court.

"(2) In January of the 23rd Year (1934) of the Chinese Republic, the accused, by means of intimidation, extorted a sum of $67,000 from one Loh Kwan Tseng (陸冠曾). The facts are as follows:- Despite their separation which had been effected a long time before, Loh Chu Shang (陸翥雙), the uncle of Loh Kwan Tseng, appointed Sung Sao Ching to secure payment of $67,000 from Loh Kwan Tseng by means of prosecution and threats. In addition to the accused, Wong Tseng Chuen and Kiang Chao Chow (江肇周) both took part in this case as mediators. Loh Kwan Tseng and his accountants named Yui Sao Ching (俞少卿) and Pan Hui Tseng (潘煥丞) are now present in Court."

昨日下午，上海第一特区地方法院审判长钱鸿业（钱鸿业）再次开庭审理前工部局警务处刑事侦缉队（C.D.C.）队员孙少卿涉嫌敲诈勒索及包揽诉讼一案。

助理市检察官Paul Y. Ru向法庭陈述道：“关于此前针对被告指控的敲诈吴登瀛一案，市警察现已查明受害人吴登瀛支付的本票数量及金额，以及兑付该本票的钱庄名称。将编制详细陈述提交法庭。与被告人孙少卿敲诈徐懋昌一案有关的主要人物徐懋昌和潘雪艳均在庭。已获取与‘姚志春案’有关的合同原件，上面有孙少卿的签名。市警察现对被告提出以下额外指控：-

“(1) 中华民国二十二年（1933年）十二月某时，被告通过胁迫手段，从施德之先生处敲诈得40,000元。事实如下：- 在此之前不久，施德之辞退了一名苦力。该被辞退的苦力以济善医院的名义，与被告孙少卿、王振川、樊良伯、吴云甫等人勾结，在上海地方法院对施德之提起诉讼，声称施制造的霍乱预防液是模仿他们发明的施道世霍乱预防液。在这起诉讼过程中，他们甚至对施德之及其律师徐士浩采取胁迫行为，从而从受害人处获取了40,000元。当时，施德之的女婿‘罗勃斯’（音译）先生已向静安寺捕房通报了他们的非法行为。

“当时捕房记录的笔录现呈交法庭查阅。

“(2) 中华民国二十三年（1934年）一月，被告通过恐吓手段，从陆冠曾处敲诈得67,000元。事实如下：- 尽管陆冠曾与其叔父陆翥双早已分居，陆翥双仍委任孙少卿通过诉讼和威胁手段向陆冠曾索取67,000元。除被告外，王振川和江肇周也作为调解人参与了此案。陆冠曾及其会计师俞少卿、潘焕丞现在庭。”

After his return from Japan, he asked me for a loan of $100,000 for the establishment of a bank to be known as Hwa Chung (華中) or Hwa ---(華---) Bank, but I refused because I learned from enquiries that it was not his proposal. Yui Sao Ching was also mentioned as a defendant in this prosecution. At that time I appointed lawyer Tsai Nieh Pei (蔡倪培) to represent me in Court. As I was then residing at Soochow and in this respect I was not subject to the jurisdiction of the Shanghai District Court, Mr. Tsai told me that it was not necessary for me to attend Court. Unexpectedly, however, Yui Sao Ching was ordered to furnish security at the first hearing and to effect my appearance in Court within three days. THE CHARGES AGAINST SUNG SAO CHING

Recently, Sung Sao Ching (孫少卿) (an ex-C.D.C. of the S.M.P.), native of Tungchow, was arrested by Assistant Superintendent Loh Lien Kwei and D.I. Liu Chao Kwei of the Municipal Police on charges of fraud and contracting the management of lawsuits of another. He was arraigned before the Shanghai First Special District Court on the following day and was charged under Articles 157 and 346 of the Chinese Criminal Code for having contracted the management of a case of division of property affecting Wu Teng Ying (吳登瀛) and Sung Wu Kwei Tseng (孫吳桂貞).

On the afternoon of March 9, Presiding Judge Chien Hung Nieh (錢鴻業) of the First Special District Court resumed the hearing of the case.

Addressing the Court, Assistant Municipal Advocate Paul Ru said :- "In addition to the charge dealt with at the previous hearing, the Municipal Police now bring the following additional charges against the accused:-

1) Yao Yoeh Poo (姚月波), native of South Tungchow, owner of the Yao Jen Shing Building Contractor Company (姚仁興營造廠), sometime ago entered into a joint contract for a certain building with his brother Yao Jen Nyi (姚仁義), owner of the Yao Zung Shing Building Contractor Company (姚宗興營造廠). Later Yao Jen Nyi died and his son Yae Tse Tsung (姚慈春) carried on his father's business. In 1931, Yao Yoeh Poo desired to settle accounts with his nephew for the contracting of the building, and asked the nephew to pay him a sum of $10,000. Yao Tse Tsung refused to pay the money and entrusted the accused Sung Sao Ching with the negotiations. The accused then asked one Doctor Tse Nan San (朱南山) to mediate. As a result, the case was peacefully settled for a sum of $5,000, of which Yao Yoeh Poo received $1,500 only.

2) In December, 1935, the well known actress Pan Sih Yen (潘雪艷), residing in house No. 2, Dong Foh Li (同福里), Rue Ratard, French Concession, asked the accused Sung Sao Ching to extort a sum of $20,000 from one Hsu Mou Chong (徐慕忠), owner of the Dah Foong Cotton Mill (大豐紗廠), the younger brother of Hsu Mou Daung (徐慕棟), compradores of the P & O Banking Corporation. Through the efforts of lawyer Wu Lin Kwen (吳麟坤), who was retained by Hsu, the case was settled for $19,000. The actress Pan received only a very small sum of money.

"Witness Yao Yoeh Poo and lawyers Wu Lin Kwen and Koo Kung Ping (顧公秉) are present in Court. Lawyer Chen Ting Sui (陳定綏) is unable to appear owing to sickness".

The statement made by witness Yao Yoeh Poo was then presented.

Addressing Wu Sung Pah (吳松柏), the son of Wu Teng Ying, the Judge said: "This Court has made enquiries of your lawyer Chen Ting Sui and he states that prior to the settlement of your case, you had received a threatening telephone message and certain persons had followed your motor car".

The witness Wu Sung Pah denied all this.

针对孙少卿的指控

近期，通州籍人士、前工部局警务处华人侦探主任（C.D.C.）孙少卿（Sung Sao Ching），因涉嫌诈骗及包揽他人诉讼，被工部局警务处副督察长罗连贵（Loh Lien Kwei）及侦探刘朝贵（Liu Chao Kwei）逮捕。次日，他被提解至上海第一特区地方法院受审，并被控违反《中华民国刑法》第157条及第346条，罪名是包揽涉及吴登瀛（Wu Teng Ying）和孙吴桂贞（Sung Wu Kwei Tseng）的析产案件。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, March 2, 1937

Legal-Racket Expose
Due As Ex-Detective
Faces Extortion Count

Judge Dzien Determined To Smash Shyster Ring
Preying On Civil Suit Participants; Silk
Taipan Said Victimized By Blackmail

Litigations Declared Engineered

THE first gun in what promises to develop into a sensational expose of a shyster-lawyer, legal-racket, blackmail ring, that has existed in Shanghai for a number of years, was fired in the First District Court this morning when Sung Sau-ching, 47, former detective of the Shanghai Municipal Police, was charged with extorting $40,000 from Mr. Wu Tung-ying, wealthy proprietor of a silk filature on Miller Road.

With Chief Judge Dzien expressing himself as determined to smash the shyster group whose existence is said to be known to almost every lawyer in Shanghai, further charges of muscling in on civil suits in Shanghai involving hundreds of thousands of dollars are expected to be laid against Sung within the next few weeks.

SETTLED TO OWN PROFIT

Evidence is piling up that Sung and a group of lawyers, in addition to a melange of loafers and racketeers, have insinuated themselves into legitimate law suits as well as trumped-up cases, including a well-known rape case involving a wealthy Chinese merchant several years ago and numerous other cases that Sung and his group are alleged to have settled out of court to their own profit.

Recently, an alleged former associate of Sung sent a letter to the First District Court requesting that Sung had obtained money from him by illegal means. Sung retaliated with the same charge against his former associate. Judge Dzien, anxious to get to the bottom of what had been a four-year-old mystery, ordered both men to appear before him. Last week Sung was brought before the judge and remanded in custody on suspicion of committing a breach Article 356 of the Chinese Criminal Code which states that: "Whosoever, with intent to make profit, incites or contrives for the commencement of any lawsuit, or another, shall be punished with imprisonment for not more than one year, or detention or a fine of not more than five hundred yuan."

Extortion Charged

This morning, however, a charge of extortion was preferred against Sung. Hearing testimony of Misses Sung, by her father, Mr. Wu Tung-ying, it was alleged that a sister of Mr. Wu Tung-ying was intimidated by Sung to try and get money from her brother.

（印：FILE 4/3）
（批：DSR 2/3）

S. D. REGIST
S. B. D. 2819
Date 4 3 37

Mediation Offered

With the sister threatening to bring the suit to court, Sung and lawyers offered to mediate the case. At first they demanded $300,000, but later reduced this demand to $120,000. The son of Mr. Wu told his father not to pay this amount as it was exorbitant. Finally a sum of $60,-000 was paid, but of this amount the sister obtained only $12,000.

She did not know how much had been claimed by the lawyers and Sung, but thinking that her brother had settled for more she wrote a letter to her brother's native guild and asked them to look into the matter. The sister finally learned that her brother had given her $40,000, when he learned that she had not received this amount he refused to do anything about it.

Taking His Time

The matter might have rested there, but Judge Dzien became interested in Sung's activities. This morning the judge cleared the courtroom of spectators and told Sung to speak out.

"You have nothing to fear. You've told police about your activities and you have no reason to deny them here."

Hearings against Sung were remanded to next week and Judge Dzien indicated that he wished to take ample time with charges, bringing them up one by one and exploring all their possibilities.

It is known that Sung was connected with a lawyer's office on Rue August Boppe and that another office had been set up West Gate Road.

In simple terms, Sung is believed to have extorted money from rich people by stirring up litigations.

法律勒索团伙曝光
前侦探面临敲诈指控

迪岑法官决心捣毁讼棍团伙
该团伙专门猎食民事诉讼参与者；据称丝绸大亨遭勒索

诉讼被指系人为操纵

今天上午，在第一特区地方法院，打响了有望揭露一个在上海存在多年的讼棍律师、法律勒索及敲诈团伙的第一枪。47岁的上海公共租界工部局警务处前侦探宋少卿（Sung Sau-ching）被控从米勒路（Miller Road）一位富有的丝厂老板吴登瀛（Wu Tung-ying）先生那里敲诈了40,000美元。

首席法官迪岑（Dzien）表示决心粉碎这个讼棍集团，据说上海几乎每位律师都知道该集团的存在。预计在未来几周内，将对宋某提出更多指控，涉及其插手上海数十万美元的民事案件。

为私利而和解

证据不断累积，显示宋某与一群律师，以及一帮闲散人员和勒索者混迹在一起，他们不仅渗入合法的诉讼案件，还参与捏造的案件，包括几年前一起涉及一名富有中国商人的著名强奸案，以及据称由宋某及其团伙庭外和解以牟取私利的众多其他案件。

最近，一名据称是宋某前同伙的人致函第一特区地方法院，请求调查宋某通过非法手段从其处获取钱财一事。宋某则以同样的指控报复其前同伙。迪岑法官急于查清这起已持续四年的谜案真相，命令两人出庭受审。上周，宋某被带至法官面前，因涉嫌违反《中华民国刑法》第356条而被还押候审。该条款规定：“意图得利，挑唆或包揽他人诉讼者，处一年以下有期徒刑、拘役或五百元以下罚金。”

被控敲诈

然而，今天上午对宋某提出了敲诈指控。在听取吴登瀛先生对其女儿宋氏姐妹的证词时，据称吴登瀛先生的妹妹受到宋某的恐吓，试图从其兄弟那里获取钱财。

（印：FILE 4/3）
（批：DSR 2/3）

S. D. REGIST
S. B. D. 2819
日期 37年3月4日

提供调解

由于该妹妹威胁要将诉讼告上法庭，宋某和律师们提出调解此案。起初他们索要300,000美元，后来将要求降至120,000美元。吴登瀛先生的儿子告诉父亲不要支付这笔款项，因为金额过高。最终支付了60,000美元，但其中该妹妹仅得到12,000美元。

她不知道律师和宋某索取了多少，但以为兄弟支付的和解金更多，便写信给其兄弟的同乡会馆，请他们调查此事。该妹妹最终得知其兄弟给了她40,000美元，当吴登瀛得知她未收到此数额后，拒绝再采取任何行动。

从容应对

此事本可能就此搁置，但迪岑法官对宋某的活动产生了兴趣。今天上午，法官清空了法庭内的旁听人员，并让宋某开口陈述。

“你没什么好怕的。你已经向警方交代了你的活动，没有理由在这里否认。”

针对宋某的审讯被延期至下周，迪岑法官表示希望有充足的时间处理各项指控，逐一提出并探究所有可能性。

据悉，宋某与奥古斯特·博佩路（Rue August Boppe）的一家律师事务所有关联，并在西门路（West Gate Road）设立了另一家事务所。

简而言之，人们认为宋某通过挑起诉讼来向富人敲诈钱财。

（印：RECD - 1937年3月3日 上海公共租界工部局警务处收）

3月2日上午10时，第一特区地方法院主审法官钱鸿业（Chien Hung Nieh）继续审理此案。

助理市政检察官保罗·鲁（Paul Ru）发表如下声明：“警方在还押期间对本案进行了详细调查。由于还押期较短，无法查明宋某包揽的所有诉讼案件。目前仅涉及再纶丝厂（Zai Lun Silk Filature）业主吴登瀛（Wu Teng Ying）与其妹孙吴氏（Sung Wu Sz，即吴桂贞 Wu Kwei Tseng）之间的财产分割案。其父未留下财产。后来，吴登瀛通过经商变得非常富有。孙吴氏通过姚月波（Yao Yoeh Poo）结识了宋少卿。宋少卿代表孙吴氏提起财产分割民事诉讼；他还以挪用公款罪对吴登瀛提起刑事诉讼，并索要200,000美元。吴登瀛答应支付120,000美元。吴登瀛之子吴松柏（Wu Sung Pah）反对这一安排。他咨询了陈廷绥（Chen Ting Sui）律师，后者成功与代表孙吴氏的律师顾公平（Koo Kung Ping）达成协议，由吴登瀛支付孙吴氏40,000美元。实际上，孙吴氏仅收到12,500美元。数年后，孙吴氏因是湖州人，向湖州会馆报告了此诉讼案。湖州会馆委员会致函吴登瀛，询问实际支付金额，吴复函会馆。警方已获取此证据。现依据《刑法》第346条指控宋少卿敲诈勒索，并依据第157条指控其包揽他人诉讼。”

经法庭讯问，吴松柏作如下陈述：“起初，我的姑母孙吴氏聘请陈春（Chen Chun）律师给我父亲写信。我请陈廷绥律师处理此案。此事在庭外和解。这40,000美元由我交给陈春律师，他随后转交给代表我姑母的顾公平律师。我从未见过名为宋少卿的人。

When questioned by the Presiding Judge, the
accused Sung Sao Ching denied all knowledge of the affair.
He said that he did not know Sung Wu Sz or Wu Sung Iah, and

the past 30 years.
When questioned by the Court whether or not he
was an opium smoker, he stated that formerly he smoked opium
but that he had already got rid of the habit.
When further asked by the Court whether he had
taken any part in the "Hsu's (徐) Case Support Committee,"
he denied any knowledge of the Committee.
